verdicts.why: Joining or increasing something, or saying something further, states an action and takes no side on it.
Arithmetic combination of numbers; purely descriptive.
Starting to speak is reported plainly; any judgement in the sentences comes from words like 'scolding', not from 'began'.
Taking the first step in an action; no attitude toward the actor or the action.
An event having a start point is a bare temporal fact.
Names a belief without proof as a matter of definition; the dismissiveness of 'just your opinion' lives in 'just', and 'good opinion' shows the word itself is neutral.
An expressed belief; the word reports the message type without approving or discounting it.
A vague but trusted idea; 'vague' is the meaning of the sense, not an attitude beyond it.
A region or location ('what part of London'); the low regard in one sentence is carried by 'such', not by 'part'.
A portion relative to a whole; as plain as 'piece' or 'section'.
'For my part' or 'one part of my conduct' marks a person's share or role without judging it.
A portion of a natural object ('the narrowest parts' of a stream); descriptive only.
A discourse adverb of correction or contrast ('rather X than Y'); it orders alternatives and aims no attitude at either.
A degree hedge like 'somewhat'; its mild lean toward unexpected or unwelcome qualities is a usage tendency about degree, not approval or contempt for the thing modified.
'Would rather' states a preference as fact; the word does not colour what is preferred or rejected.
The course of a person's existence; a plain noun for the span of one's doings.
The state of being alive, as in 'anxiety for his life'; the referent matters but the word takes no side.
A functional period ('a time of life'); a neutral measure of duration.
The faculty of thought; the condescension in 'the generality of female minds' is the sentence's, not the noun's.
A formed judgement or view; like 'opinion' it names the thing held without rating it.
Memory or recall ('bear in mind'); purely descriptive.
Going after someone or something; any suggestion of pursuit in one sentence comes from the plot, not from the verb, which is as neutral as 'come after'.
Coming after as a consequence; a bare relation of sequence and cause.
Being later in time ('a pause followed this speech'); no attitude at all.
The temporal 'now' or 'current'; locates in time and judges nothing.
